1 What Counts as Pressure? The Pre-Delivery Mathematical Framework

Cricket analytics often errs by defining pressure simply as "the death overs". In reality, a team needing 85 off 12 balls with 9 wickets down is in the 19th over, but the contest is dead (zero leverage). Conversely, 30/3 in over 5 generates immense stress.

CLUTCH-X evaluates pressure strictly on the pre-delivery match state across all 200,999 balls (IPL & T20I, 2022–2026), preventing outcome leakage:

2nd Innings (Chasing Context)

  • Required Run Rate Stress (35%): Scaled from RRR 6.0 to 18.0+.
  • Wicket Depletion (30%): Linear pressure scaling as wickets fall (0 to 10).
  • Innings Urgency (20%): Scaled with balls elapsed (0 to 120).
  • Win Prob. Leverage Index (15%): $4 \cdot WP \cdot (1 - WP)$ maximizing on 50-50 contests.

1st Innings (Target Setting Context)

  • Phase Leverage (40%): Death overs 16–20 carry maximum swing potential.
  • Collapse Deficit (35%): Excess wickets lost vs. expected run-of-play.
  • Par Deficit (25%): Lagging behind 8.50 RPO baseline par score.
  • Knockout Stakes: $1.15 imes$ multiplier for playoff and final fixtures.

2 Top 10 Batters Under Pressure: Clutch Batting Index (CBI)
